title: f83r P4-P5 complete exploratory rota pair with all 53 RAW485 meanings frozen
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED, NOT SELECTED. A new complete music reading of the fixed33-group f83r.25-30 paragraph retains every RAW485 lexical value and all14 original clauses. Six old types occur at nine new positions; eighteen new whole-form guesses cover the other24 positions under six new productions. Both full paragraphs describe one explicitly linked performance: initial leader/pes entry, silent pending rota singers, opposed pes pause locations and persistent cycles. Two new-block diplomatic forms remain unbound; IT solchedy creates a serious incompatible old meaning. No tests or automatic experiment selection.

decision_note.question: Can the entire second paragraph support an explicit music working interpretation while the existing 53 lexical entries, performer types, ENTER semantics and first full paragraph remain unchanged?
decision_note.unknown_after_primary_review: RAW485 is a complete one-paragraph hypothetical instruction program. This new block was previously used for incompatible unweaving/balneological hypotheses, not this shared music lexicon. The own review uses RAW485 and old source primaries, not GDT1022 execution details. Coherence of the new shared reading is proposed, not tested.
decision_note.changed_input: One additional already exposed complete33-group paragraph, 18 openly guessed whole forms, six productions, and an explicit same-performance reference. No old meaning, type, operator, source branch or original clause is altered.
decision_note.pass_changes: Retain a concrete two-paragraph projected music hypothesis with only six actually reused word types in the new block; do not call this verification of all53 entries or independent translation evidence.
decision_note.failure_changes: Reject the fixed new joint descendant if any old value requires reinterpretation, any participant/part must be replaced, the two initial-entry declarations create duplicate events, or the same cycle-preservation rule conflicts across U/L. Keep RAW485 and all old alternative readings unchanged.
decision_note.smallest_test: Parse all33 new groups with this fixed lexicon and six productions, combine their constraints with the unchanged62-group RAW485 program, and resolve the explicit same-performance reference. Check both initial-entry declarations against a single initial-event bank, the two NEXT_PES cursor steps, disjoint group types, upper/lower pause ownership and full joint traces for the same 2/3/4-singer and C0-C3 cases. No new corpus search or decoder. Report raw-form and IT conflicts separately.
decision_note.producer_execution: NONE. No semantic/model tests, trace calculation, current experiment-file reading or selected experiment.

original_grammar_unchanged.production_freedom: Fourteen largely one-off productions are fitted to this exposed paragraph. They are not an independently learned grammar or evidence for these readings. This deliberate exploratory freedom must remain visible.
original_grammar_unchanged.coordination_ellipsis: Only C05 inherits PAUSE into its second coordinated member. Only C08 reuses the explicitly referenced prior cue rule with new participant arguments. No other missing predicates may be inserted.
reference_conventions: FOLLOWER is a role predicate: EACH/ALL quantify it; C07 selects its first member; C11 constrains the encompassing rota group. Repetition does not create new singers.
ONE in C06 and LEADER in C07/C14 resolve the same R0.
OTHER_MEMBER in C09 resolves lower pes L from the explicitly ordered pair in C05.

EXCEPT in C14 scopes only over C13; it does not erase C04/C09 pause restrictions.
original_grammar_unchanged.roundtrip_limit: Retain each terminal and clause provenance so a parser can reconstruct the projected 62-group input exactly. A roundtrip alone is not a semantic test and does not settle the two diplomatic forms.

original_semantic_contract_unchanged.participants: Choose one of the already source-permitted cases N=2,3,4. Distinct R0..R(N-1) perform M; distinct U,L perform P1,P2. R0 is leader; Ri, i>0 are followers. A role, a physical singer, a part, and a particular event occurrence are distinct records.

original_semantic_contract_unchanged.binding_limit: These four links to the Harley source are additional unconfirmed referent assumptions. fixed_operators.SING: Execute successive note/rest events of the performer's own assigned part on that performer's local clock. Same operator for C06 leader and C09 lower pes; the argument-owned part changes the trace.
fixed_operators.REPEAT: After the complete current part, restart that part from its beginning on the same voice clock, with no added delay or new singer. Same operator for following rota singers in C02 and the two pes in C03.
fixed_operators.TOGETHER: Assert onset equality for the subject set; preserve all individual part identities and local clock trajectories.
fixed_operators.ENTER: Single inactive-to-active transition of a rota singer at its first prescribed onset. A later part repeat is not a second ENTER.
fixed_operators.WHEN: Create an event dependency using a resolved owner and cue, not a free equal-time spacing or textual adjacency relation.
fixed_operators.PAUSE: A rest is a duration-carrying event with its written owner/location. Internal versus terminal is topological, not equal-half duration.
fixed_operators.NO_END_PAUSE: Forbid an added terminal rest on P2; do not delete P2's already written internal rest.

original_semantic_contract_unchanged.phase_persistence: An ENTER on any Ri updates only that singer's active flag/start time. It cannot reset U or L, change their parts, or restart their cycles. Motif repetitions preserve participant identity.
original_semantic_contract_unchanged.leader_repeat_assumption: The main part is interpreted as a cyclic rota for every selected rota performer, including R0. The owned source packet calls this the ordinary rota reading. It is an explicit source interpretation, not a separately identified target REPEAT word for the leader.
original_semantic_contract_unchanged.written_pause_scope: C04 restricts follower rest positions; C10 assigns source longa duration to all rota written rests. The assigned M supplies the same written pauses for R0. Extending numeric longa realization to pes is only the old source-branch assumption, not a new conclusion from C10.
original_semantic_contract_unchanged.duration_policy: Use the four exact documentary_duration_branches in ROTA_SOURCE_EVENTS.json separately. Keep all their qualifications, C2 prose/score disagreement and C3 constructed attribution sensitivity. No branch optimization, Cartesian-product expansion or certified historical rhythm claim.
original_semantic_contract_unchanged.need_and_window: The source fixes no finite stop or repeat count. For a bounded diagnostic hold the common need flag true through [0, last_entry + lcm(M_period,P1_period,P2_period)). This is an observation window, not a source-prescribed performance ending. Include complete event pairs crossing the boundary with clipping separately labeled; compare startup and at least one common period after all entries.
original_semantic_contract_unchanged.complete_source_scope: The hypothetical account covers every operative rule R01-R07 plus explicit consequences about early entry and leader exception. It does not translate either lyric, syllable alignment, every note name, tempo, absolute pitch, or a finite stopping command.

frozen_parent.scope: The six new productions add a new block grammar. They do not rewrite any old reduction, type, reference convention or operator. All source/meaning qualifications and unresolved old diplomatic forms remain binding.
no_generic_weakening: ENTER still denotes a single first inactive-to-active transition of a rota singer; it cannot be applied to a pes performer.
COMPANIONS remains the rota-performer group, including its leader; it is not a generic word for any fellow performer.
UPPER_PES remains U/P1 and PES remains the distinct pair [U,L] assigned P1/P2.
OTHERS_SILENT still applies to all not-yet-entered rota singers, not merely an arbitrary silent subset.
LEADER remains R0 and no later clause installs another leader.

new_grammar_contract.mode: As in the parent, the whole writing is a declarative instruction specification, not a list that performs another real event on each mention. The two blocks compile together; event execution follows their resolved temporal constraints.
new_grammar_contract.productions: Exactly the six displayed terminal-tag sequences and reductions D01-D06, using the existing word boundaries. No occurrence-specific word sense, deleted group, silent filler, new surface normalization or after-the-fact regrouping.
new_grammar_contract.explicit_cross_block_binding: The new qokylddy=SAME_PERFORMANCE_REFERENCE in D02 resolves the next explicit ROTA declaration: techedy at .31. It identifies the new local case with RAW485's case, sharing R0..R(N-1), U,L,M,P1,P2,X and T0. This singleton forward-reference meaning and direction are newly guessed; lexical agreement alone would not force shared physical performers.
new_grammar_contract.entry_event_identity: Each rota performer has one first ENTER event by the unchanged parent contract. D01 constrains ENTER(R0). D03 uses the explicit new RESTATE_SAME_STARTER marker dain to constrain that same event, not create another inactive-to-active transition. A decoder that needs a second leader or a second initial ENTER fails this fixed construction.
new_grammar_contract.begin_pes_not_ENTER: otal explicitly denotes BEGIN_BOTH_PES, yielding StartPart(U) and StartPart(L). shckhedy explicitly denotes START_NEXT_PES. Neither changes the domain of old ENTER to accompaniment performers.
new_grammar_contract.iterator_scope: D03 alone opens a fresh cursor i=0 over the inherited ordered pair [U,L]. Each shckhedy returns StartPart(pair[i]) then increments i. Its two adjacent occurrences must consume the complete pair in order, leaving i=2. No reset between them, alternative voice choice, duplicated U, body-name gloss per occurrence or extra unnamed pes is allowed. This bounded cursor scope is a new grammar assumption.
new_grammar_contract.same_time_reference: All three qokeedy occurrences refer to the identical T0, not independent free delays. Both qokeey occurrences and dain resolve the same starter whose identity with shedy/R0 is written in D02.
new_grammar_contract.co_onset_operator: Both qokedy occurrences implement one CO_ONSET operator over explicit first-start event sets. D01 compares ENTER(R0) with both pes starts; D04 compares U's first part start with ENTER(R0). This does not synchronize every later pes restart to every main-melody cycle boundary.
new_grammar_contract.same_cycle_operator: Both oldy occurrences implement PRESERVE_OWN_CYCLE(performer) using that performer's assigned part from the unchanged parent. D04 supplies U/P1; D05 supplies L/P2. No switch of parts, event order or duration branch is licensed.
new_grammar_contract.rest_modifier_scope: cheeky and cheey are properties of the whole assigned part: terminal or internal written rest. They are not commands to be silent at t=0. qody asserts that the complete assigned part's last event is not a rest; it does not delete an existing terminal rest or any internal rest. This new predicate is deliberately stated precisely; it does not modify the old kain operator.
new_grammar_contract.group_distinction: D06 treats s and okeedy as two arguments to the explicit final DISTINCT_GROUPS predicate, not an apposition or a compound meaning pes companions. Their original role types stay distinct.
new_grammar_contract.silence_time: At T0 after the prescribed simultaneous initial starts, the not-yet-entered rota singers are R1..R(N-1), a nonempty group in all inherited N=2/3/4 cases. qoky constrains all of them. Pes and active R0 are not reclassified as pending rota singers.
new_grammar_contract.inverse_limit: Retain every projected terminal and source locator. Roundtrip coverage is not semantic accuracy and does not bind four diplomatic uncertainties across the pair.
new_grammar_contract.event_bank: Use unique typed first-event keys ENTER(r) for rota singers and FIRST_PART_START(v,assigned(v)) for part starts. BEGIN_BOTH_PES and the two iterator outputs reference the same U/L first-event keys in D01/D03. RESTATE reasserts their common onset, rather than executing additional starts.
new_grammar_contract.plural_group_binding: In D06 the bare plural COMPANIONS denotes the extent of the unchanged rota-performer role among the existing N participants. This noun-to-group binding is a new clause-construction choice, not a change to the lexical human-performer type or an inclusion of pes.

minimal_new_operator_contract.INITIAL_ONSET: A TIME reference T0 belonging to the explicitly shared performance.
minimal_new_operator_contract.CO_ONSET(A,B): Require every first-start event in nonempty typed sets A and B to have equal time; no identity fusion or later phase reset.
minimal_new_operator_contract.BEGIN_BOTH_PES(pair): Return the two first StartPart event terms for the fixed pair [U,L], preserving their P1/P2 assignments.
minimal_new_operator_contract.START_NEXT_PES(pair,i): For 0<=i<2 return (StartPart(pair[i]),i+1); at i=2 a further call is undefined. The written two calls are not hardcoded to two unrelated names.
minimal_new_operator_contract.PRESERVE_OWN_CYCLE(v): Use assigned(v)'s complete ordered note/rest sequence and retained branch durations. The onset established for v determines later cycle boundaries. Other singers' ENTER events do not modify that cycle or clock.
minimal_new_operator_contract.IMMEDIATE_CYCLE_RESTART(v): At completion of assigned(v), restart it on v's existing clock without an added terminal rest, under the parent's unchanged need condition.
minimal_new_operator_contract.DISTINCT_GROUPS(A,B): Require A intersect B to be empty; preserve both already bound performer groups.
minimal_new_operator_contract.RESTATE: Reassert constraints on the same previously identified event term. It does not run an event again.
minimal_new_operator_contract.IDENTICAL_ROLE(a,b): Assert identity of same-sort HUMAN_PERFORMER referents, not similarity of names or parts.
minimal_new_operator_contract.WITHOUT_TERMINAL_REST(part): Require that the last event in the complete assigned written cycle is not REST. Do not delete, move or relabel any source event. P2 satisfies the source condition; an assigned cycle ending in REST does not.

source_scope.new_block_content: A complete hypothetical explanatory prelude about R03 startup, the R02 distinction between rota and pes singers, and R06/R07 opposed pause/repeat behavior. It reuses the source already bound by RAW485; it does not introduce another score, song, source witness or performer.

No universal harmony law, tempo, finite repeat count or source-prescribed stopping time.
Upper-terminal-pause classification and source verb-expansion cautions remain as in the original packet.
The source's ordinary cyclic interpretation of the leader's main part remains an assumption; the new text does not independently prove it.
